Missing construction, not a constructor idiom: Rails' `initialize` (actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/http/request.rb:64-75) builds `@rack_request = Rack::Request.new(env)` and exposes it via `attr_reader :rack_request` (:77). The port (http/request.ts:148-158) copies `env` and fills in Rack defaults Rails does not set; the wrapper is built lazily by an invented `get rackRequest()` that caches it in `env["action_dispatch.rack_request"]` (http/request.ts:925-931), so the constructor never constructs one. Not tracked by a story: actionpack is outside the project's stated focus (activerecord and its dependencies), which is why the convergence story filed for this row was closed as out of scope.

request.rb:212-221 makes `method` the PRE-override HTTP method, read from `rack.methodoverride.original_method` before `REQUEST_METHOD`; trails inverts the pair — `method` applies an override it reads from `HTTP_X_HTTP_METHOD_OVERRIDE`/`_method` inline, and `requestMethod` is the raw value. Converging needs both readers and the override site moved, tracked as story converge-request-method-onto-methodoverride-original-method.
